title: Weft
tagline: Real-time collaborative editor with CRDT-backed offline support.
summary: A document editor that stays usable offline and converges cleanly when you reconnect. Built on Yjs with a custom binding layer for rich-text and a Rust backend for persistence.
body:
## Why

Most "collaborative" editors fall apart the moment your wifi drops. Weft treats offline as a first-class state, not an error.

## How

The client is a thin React shell over a Yjs document. Edits propagate through a WebRTC mesh when peers are reachable, falling back to a Rust relay that buffers updates and forwards them on reconnect. The relay stores compressed snapshots in Postgres so cold starts are fast.

## What I learned

CRDTs are easy to reason about until you add formatting. Then they're hard. The fix was modeling marks as separate metadata streams instead of inline attributes.

title: Wearable EEG Headband
tagline: Dry-electrode 4-channel EEG with onboard ML inference.
summary: A discreet headband that captures EEG without conductive gel and runs lightweight inference on-device for focus-state classification. Streams summaries — not raw signal — over BLE to preserve privacy.

title: Pageant
tagline: Build-time full-text search for static sites — zero runtime servers.
summary: A small CLI that indexes your static site at build time and ships a tiny WASM searcher so users get instant search without a backend. Indexes typically compress to under 100KB for sites with thousands of pages.

title: Open-Source UV-Vis Spectrometer
tagline: Sub-$200 spectrometer with replaceable diffraction grating.
summary: A teaching-grade spectrometer designed for undergrad chem labs. Linear CCD, machined aluminum body, USB-C interface, with calibration software that runs in the browser.
